# Typed DTOs over Array Shapes

Use `final readonly class` DTOs instead of `@phpstan-type array{...}` shapes (or bare `array $data` params) when data crosses class boundaries.

## Naming Convention

- **Input DTOs** (data going into an operation/handler): suffix `Transfer` — e.g. `CreateScorecardTransfer`.
- **Handler return DTOs** (data coming out of a handler): suffix `Result` — e.g. `CreateScorecardResult`.
- Never use a `T` prefix on PHP DTOs — the `T` prefix is reserved for TypeScript types on the frontend.

## Rule

- When data flows through **2+ methods** or is passed to **another class**, create a `final readonly class` DTO.
- `@phpstan-type array{...}` is only acceptable for single-method local use (e.g. the return type of a private method consumed in one place within the same class).
- Never use `@phpstan-import-type` — if a type must be shared, it must be a class.

## Why

- PHPStan array shapes are invisible to IDEs — no autocomplete, no refactoring support.
- `@phpstan-import-type` creates fragile, non-obvious coupling between classes.
- `array $data` parameters hide the contract — the real shape lives only in a docblock.
- Typed DTOs give runtime safety, IDE support, and self-documenting APIs.

## Pattern

```php
// Bad — PHPStan-only type alias passed as a bare array
/** @phpstan-type ScorecardData array{id?: string|null, title?: string|null} */
final readonly class Importer { /* ... */ }

// Good — typed DTO
final readonly class ImportScorecardTransfer {
    public function __construct(
        public ?string $id = null,
        public ?string $title = null,
    ) {}
}
```

## Boundary Conversion

When data enters the module as an untyped array (e.g. from an external API), convert at the boundary with a static `fromArray()` factory:

```php
public static function fromArray(array $data): self
{
    return new self(
        id: $data['id'] ?? null,
        title: $data['title'] ?? null,
    );
}
```
